newsitem.title: URUGUAY: SOCCER-ARCH-RIVALS URUGUAY AND ARGENTINA DRAW 0-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARCH-RIVALS URUGUAY AND ARGENTINA DRAW 0-0.

text.p: Old foes Uruguay and Argentina played to a 0-0 draw in a crucial South American World Cup qualifying match on Sunday.
Uruguay, backed by a 68,000 crowd in the Centenario stadium, created the better chances in a match that, despite the stalemate, produced plenty of excitement, especially in the second half.
The result was a huge relief for Argentine coach Daniel Passarella, who has seen his team drop home points against Paraguay and Chile and lose away to unfancied Ecuador.
Argentina, who brought in the experience of Diego Simeone and veteran Nestor Gorosito for the game, stayed third in the single South American World Cup group, ahead of Uruguay on goal difference.
The top four of the nine teams qualify for the 1998 World Cup in France.

Passarella was clearly happy with the result. "We overcame a stiff test and kept third place in a very tough qualifying contest," he said. His counterpart Juan Ahuntchain said: "Uruguay played better and had more chances."

The best news for Passarella was the sound performance of goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez, the fifth player he has used in the position in the last six months in what has become an increasingly desperate search.
Gonzalez began well, producing a spectacular save to push away a goalbound header from Uruguayan veteran Enzo Francescoli in the seventh minute.

Uruguay, who were meeting their arch-rivals from across the River Plate for the first time in a World Cup qualifier, had a penalty appeal turned down in the 20th minute when striker Daniel Fonseca claimed he had been fouled.
Argentina looked somewhat lethargic in the first half and striker Ariel Ortega, the one bright spot of their 1-1 draw at home to Chile last month, was again the only player to look dangerous.
The away team were more aggressive in the second half, when their best chance fell to substitute striker Hernan Crespo, who saw his 67th minute effort well-saved by goalkeeper Robert Siboldi.
Uruguay forced a series of corners as they mounted a desperate last offensive in the dying minutes but they were unable to find a way past Gonzalez.

Uruguay - 1-Robert Siboldi, 2-Washington Tais, 4-Jose Herrera, 3-Paolo Montero, 6-Gustavo Mendez, 5-Eber Moas, 18- Gabriel Cedres, 8-Pablo Bengoechea, 7-Nelson Abeijon, 10-Enzo Francescoli (17-Alvaro Recoba, 69th minute), 9-Daniel Fonseca (13-Sergio Abreu, 57th).

Argentina - 1-Ignacio Gonzlez, 4-Nelson Vivas, 6-Pablo Paz, 2-Roberto Sensini, 3-Jose Chamot, 8-Diego Simeone, 5-Matias Almeyda, 11-Nestor Gorosito (17-Hernan Crespo, 56th), 7- Christian Bassedas, 10-Ariel Ortega, 9-Gabriel Batistuta.
